what should i do during an earthquake.answer:
• Drop down to your knees and make yourself small, cover your head and neck, and protect your face [1]
• If indoors, practice drop, cover, hold until the shaking stops and you are sure it is safe to exit [1]
• If you are travelling in a vehicle, pull off the road to a clear area, stop the vehicle, and apply parking brake [1]
• If you are near an exit point, quickly move outside and stand in open space [1]
• Cover your head and neck with one arm and hand, and hold on to a sturdy table or desk for shelter [2]

what should i do if a building catches f.answer:
• STOP, DROP and ROLL if clothes catch fire [1]
• Conduct regular drills to prepare for fire [1]
• Get your premises fire audited and check for loose electric connections [2]
• Dial 101 in case of fire [2]
• Lay down/sit near the floor if trapped, curtail entry of smoke into the room, look for exit [2]

what precautions should i take during a.answer:
• Seal entry points around doors and vents, and seal windows if water is likely to rise that high [1]
• Do not drive in flood water as it can wash away even big vehicles [2]
• Stay away from electric poles and fallen power lines to avoid electrocution [2]
• Wash hands with soap and water before eating food or feeding young ones [2]
• Use disinfectants to keep your surroundings clean [2]

what are the basic firstaid steps for an.answer:
• Apply tourniquet above injury, document time of application, check responsiveness, and pulse [1]
• Check airway is open and self-maintained, and perform head-tilt chin-lift and Uaw thrust if trauma [1]
• Assess breathing, and perform BVM ventilations if no or inadequate breathing [1]
• Assess circulation, and provide oxygen as needed [1]
• Immobilize cervical spine if indicated [1]
